records.text: Lululemon recognizes net revenue when performance obligations are satisfied through the transfer of control of promised goods or services to customers, meaning the customer has the ability to direct the use of, and obtain substantially all of the benefits from, the product [1][2]. Control transfer includes the transfer of legal title, physical possession, the risks and rewards of ownership, and customer acceptance [1][2]. Specifically, revenue from company-operated stores and other retail locations is recognized at the point of sale, while e-commerce revenue, sales to wholesale accounts, and in-home fitness hardware sales are recognized upon receipt by the customer [1][2]. In arrangements where payment is received before the customer receives the promised good, the payment is initially recorded as deferred revenue and recognized as revenue once control transfers to the customer [1][2]. Revenue is reported net of markdowns and discounts, sales taxes collected on behalf of taxing authorities, and returns, with an allowance for estimated returns also factored into the net revenue presentation [1][2].
